overall: The AG found the Board violated the OML by failing to publicly identify the collective bargaining unit and the litigation claimant before its July 15, 2014 executive session; the litigation purpose itself was proper and the privilege question was not reached.

allegations.summary: Board entered executive session on July 15, 2014 without first publicly identifying the collective bargaining unit it was negotiating with.
allegations.key_passage: Because the Board failed to demonstrate that the purpose for the executive session would have been compromised by its disclosure of the bargaining unit with which it was in negotiation, the Board’s withholding of that information violated the Open Meeting Law.

allegations.summary: Board did not publicly identify the property-damage claimant or property before entering executive session on threatened litigation.
allegations.key_passage: We therefore find that including this minimal amount of information - the name of the claimant or the location of the property- was required, because it would have notified interested parties that this matter was being discussed behind closed doors but would not have compromised the substance of the Board’s confidential discussion regarding its litigation strategy.

allegations.summary: Complaint alleged the Board improperly used the litigation purpose (Purpose 3) to discuss potential litigation, including a sewer plant insurance claim.
Complaint alleged the Board improperly invoked attorney-client privilege as a purpose for the July 15, 2014 executive session.
allegations.key_passage: Because we find that the executive session was proper under Purpose 3, we do not need to decide whether the attomey/client privilege would have provided a valid basis for the executive session in the absence of that cited purpose.

remedy: Immediate and future compliance with the Open Meeting Law, with a caution that a similar future violation may be considered evidence of an intentional violation.

Amend the July 15, 2014 open session minutes to include the identity of the collective bargaining units and the property-damage litigation matter discussed in executive session, within 30 days of receipt of the letter.
remedy_passage: We order the Board’s immediate and future compliance with the Open Meeting Law and caution the Board that a similar future violation may be considered evidence of an intentional violation of the Law. Additionally, we order the Board to amend its July 15, 2014 open session meeting minutes to include the identity of the collective bargaining units and the litigation matter involving property damage that it discussed in executive session.
